title: 90-day lighthouse and dark scenarios playbook v0.1
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, operational playbook for the next 90 days: a light-weight lighthouse for company priorities, a short OKR draft set for exec review, and three ‘dark scenarios’ (glide / stall / storm) with concrete escalation triggers and immediate response playbooks. Use this for leadership sync, the next all-hands, and as an input to product & capacity planning.

How to use this doc:
- Read top-level OKRs and owner assignments.
- Review scenario triggers (section below). If a trigger fires, the first point of contact is the owner listed in the KR.
- All-hands: use the Run of Show for a concise update and 10-minute Q&A.

I. Top-level Objective (North Star)
Objective (Q1–Q2 focus): Make inference predictable and economical for paying customers at scale — reduce tail latency variability by 30% and reduce per-1000-token cost by 12% for hosted API traffic.

Proposed OKRs (draft):
O1: Improve runtime predictability and cost efficiency
KR1.1: Reduce 95th-percentile token latency across hosted API by 30% (baseline: 420ms) — owner: Drew Ramirez
KR1.2: Reduce average per-1k-token CPU/GPU cost by 12% via batching/quant proposals (owner: Applied ML team lead - Sofia Alvarez)
KR1.3: Deploy KV-prefix cache for top 50 routes and measure 20% token savings (owner: Serving Runtime - Morgan Patel)

O2: Expand Dedicated/Private adoption without increasing operations load
KR2.1: Close 4 new Dedicated contracts (≥$200k ARR each) with SLA add-ons (owner: Sales lead - Lina Kapoor)
KR2.2: Reduce Dedicated onboarding time from signed contract to first serving by 40% (baseline 30 days) — owner: Solutions Eng
KR2.3: Publish a Private deployment hardened checklist and runbook with 3 customers (owner: Private Deployments PM)

O3: Keep developer experience friction low as we optimize for cost
KR3.1: Shipping three frictionless SDK beta features (streaming, structured outputs, tool-calls) with <5% bug rate in GA testing — owner: DevEx
KR3.2: Reduce average time-to-first-successful-call (new signups) by 25% — owner: Developer Experience

II. All-hands Run of Show (15–20min)
- 0:00–0:02 Intro, quick wins (CEO)
- 0:02–0:07 Metrics lighthouse: latency, cost per 1k, customer adoption heatmap (VP Eng)
- 0:07–0:12 Product & Launch slate (PM) — planned Dedicated rollouts, private deployment pilots
- 0:12–0:15 Operational posture & contingencies (SRE/Platform) — quick summary of dark scenarios and where we are
- 0:15–0:20 3 quick asks from leadership (hiring, budget, prioritization) + 10m Q&A via Slido
Notes for presenters:
- Keep slides to 6 maximum. 1 slide = lighthouse metrics snapshot; 1 slide = OKRs & owner list; 1 slide = scenario triggers + immediate asks.
- Bring one demo: KV-prefix cache simulation or a short trace showing latency improvement.

III. Dark Scenarios + Triggers (explicit decision triggers and immediate actions)
1) Glide (slow downward drift in activation metrics)
Trigger: 10% week-over-week drop in new paid routes or <80% of target token volume for two consecutive weeks.
Immediate actions (0–72h):
- Growth: fast funnel audit; pause any non-essential GTM campaigns (owner: Growth lead)
- Product: run prioritized latency regressions and revert last 2 at-risk rollouts (owner: Product)
- Comm: prepare customer note template about stability focus (owner: CS lead)
Decision window: 7 days to decide either to double down on runway (budget ask) or re-scope planned feature launches.

2) Stall (operational capacity friction impacting SLAs)
Trigger: sustained P95 latency >2x SLA for >24h or 3 customer incidents tied to capacity in 7 days.
Immediate actions (0–24h):
- Activate capacity surge plan (burst Dedicated pools, route lower-tier traffic to cheaper model variants); owner: SRE
- Enable automatic fallback to compatible model variants (DevEx + Runtime)
- Weekly exec checkpoint and daily standup until resolved
Escalation: If unresolved after 48h, narrow traffic by cohort and activate compensation/retention offers for affected customers (owner: CS).

3) Storm (rapid revenue or reputational shock — e.g., data-exfil, critical outage)
Trigger: confirmed security incident affecting customer data or major outage >8h impacting >30% of customers.
Immediate actions (0–4h):
- Incident lead declared (SecOps/SRE) and Exec War Room called (CEO + CRO + CS + SecOps)
- Stop all non-essential changes, freeze deploys, engage legal and privacy teams
- Triage customer communication cadence (owner: communications)
Decision windows: continuous exec assessment; next steps include public statement, detailed RCA cadence, and compensation planning.

IV. Headcount & Budget Contingencies (simple rules)
- Hiring freeze trigger: runway forecast shows <5 months at current burn OR if Glide triggers and lead metrics drop 10% Q/Q.
- Critical hires threshold: hiring for SRE and Applied ML remains approved if Stall/Storm triggers occur.
- Temporary reallocation: conversion of two contract ICs into short-term SRE/ops shifts for 6–8 weeks on high priority in case of Stall.

V. Runbook snippets (owners + Slack playbook keywords)
- Latency regression rollback run: @drew-ops, runbook: ops/latency-rollback (slack: #ops-rollouts)
- KV-cache feature toggles: @morgan-pr, feature flags: kvcache-50routes, playbook: runtime/kvcache-toggle
- Customer incident template: cs/incidents/standard-ack

VI. Leadership asks (what we need from execs now)
- Approval for a $400k temporary capacity buffer for Q2 (covers burst Dedicated capacity & 3rd-party caching nodes) — owner: Finance + VP Eng
- Prioritization nod: pause 2 medium-scope features that conflict with batching/latency work for a 6-week period
- Exec presence: 15 minutes at the all-hands to signal prioritization focus

VII. Decision log & open questions (short list)
- Decision: whether to fund the $400k buffer — due Feb 20 (owner: CFO)
- Open Q: acceptable customer compensation model if Stall persists >72 hours (owner: CS leadership)
- Open Q: runway sensitivity assumptions — need updated forecast from Finance by Feb 5

VIII. Action list (next 7 days)
- Draft all-hands slide deck (Avery + VP Eng) — due Feb 6
- Run KV-prefix simulation on canary traffic and produce 1-slide result (Morgan) — due Feb 4
- Finance to model $400k buffer and a 3-scenario P&L (CFO) — due Feb 7
- Growth to prepare funnel audit skeleton (Lina) — due Feb 5

IX. Appendix: quick-start checklists for scenario owners
- Glide checklist: funnel diagnostics, product re-prior, comms plan, repurpose hiring freeze draft
- Stall checklist: capacity surge runbook, fallout ledger, customer retention offers ready, daily ops update cadence
- Storm checklist: incident declaration template, legal/PR play, customer data impact mapper

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact and action-oriented — the aim is to ship a minimal, shared mental model for the next 90 days and to give the all-hands an obvious set of asks and indicators.
- Please comment in-line in the Confluence page and add any changes to the decision log; if you are an owner above, ping me in #company-ops and I will slot you into the Q1 roadmap session.
